text: It also extends cellar-door provisions beyond wineries, to breweries and distilleries. Currently, wineries are the only alcohol producers who can charge for samples without holding an on-licence.
explanation: Accurate description of the existing winery cellar-door exception relative to breweries/distilleries.

text: However, we must also maintain public trust and confidence, that has been undermined by unsustainable net migration, inadequate checks and balances in 2022 and 2023, record migrant exploitation over that time, and residence decisions in 2021 that waived the usual English and health requirements and gave residence to over 230,000 people.
explanation: She herself later corrects the figure to 'nearly 213,000', so the 'over 230,000' claim here is overstated by ~17,000.

text: It was extraordinary that there had been only 47 visits when 13,000 people had been given an exemption from home-schooling, and he asked, "How do we know that any of these kids are getting a good education?" The answer from Jan Tinetti at the time, in 2023, was "I don't think that we do.", and yet they did absolutely nothing about it.
explanation: Cites specific figures (47 visits, 13,000 exemptions) and a quote; plausible but selectively framed.

text: The 2024 ERO or Education Review Office report statistics speak for themselves: 70 percent of employers did not consider NCEA level 1 to be credible; 60 percent of teachers didn’t think it was a reliable measure of what students know and can do; half of parents and 40 percent of students don’t understand how the system works.
explanation: Attributes specific figures to a named ERO report; plausible and sourced but unverified here.

text: Granting international student places is a very different thing than making sure that there are jobs here for New Zealanders. I would also like to note that we have not, for a very long time—as long as I can remember—relied on caps for any student numbers. We have a range of different levers
explanation: Accurate that NZ has not used hard caps on student numbers, relying instead on settings like funds and qualifications.

text: The 2022 Programme for International Student Assessment results released this week show a decline in the performance of 15-year-old students in maths compared to 2018 and confirm the long-term trend of declining achievement in core subjects.
explanation: PISA 2022 did show a maths decline for NZ 15-year-olds versus 2018, consistent with a long-term downward trend — accurate.

text: This bill makes a series of changes which will free New Zealanders and businesses from the stranglehold of red tape and support economic growth.
explanation: Names a bill but the benefit ('stranglehold of red tape') is sloganeering.

text: Many New Zealanders who have bought or sold a house, tried to open a bank account for their child, or needed an accountant for small business have run into anti - money-laundering red tape. It’s added cost, delays, and headaches to basic low-risk financial transactions without effectively deterring serious financial crime. These reforms cut paperwork and duplication... One example is relaxing customer due diligence requirements for lower-risk family trusts.
explanation: Concrete examples of affected transactions and a named change (family-trust due diligence), though without figures.

text: Under this bill, a customer will be allowed one serving of alcohol, limited to once per day. It reduces compliance cost, while maintaining all existing safeguards against serving minors or intoxicated persons.
explanation: Concrete limit (one serving, once per day) and a stated effect, though the magnitude of cost reduction is unquantified.

text: The bill limits objections to those who live or work in the local council area or within 1 kilometre of the proposed licence... In one case, a venue spent $45,000 preparing for a hearing that the objector didn't even turn up for.
explanation: Concrete mechanism (1 km / same council area) plus a dollar figure example.

text: The District Court criminal backlog has decreased by the largest ever reduction—a 22 percent drop over 12 months. That's 1,500 fewer cases going through the District Court.
explanation: Precise percentage, timeframe and case count.

text: We are committed to raising achievement and we’re not just talking about it; we’re doing it.
explanation: Slogan-like closing with no figure or mechanism in this sentence.

text: This work has been shaped by extensive sector engagement; more than 10,000 New Zealanders took part in consultation, alongside detailed input from a principal advisory group and sector experts.
explanation: Quantifies consultation (10,000+ participants) and names advisory structures.

text: Well, this is exactly why we are going to remove those provisions and consider them in future legislation... this Government has been providing an enormous amount more choice when it comes to education provision and specialist provision by building the first two new specialist schools in 50 years and around 40 satellite classrooms, which were provided in the previous two Budgets.
explanation: Names concrete deliverables: two specialist schools, ~40 satellite classrooms across two Budgets.

text: I have set a very ambitious target of getting 80 percent of our kids to curriculum by the time they leave intermediate.
explanation: Concrete numeric target (80%) with a defined milestone (by end of intermediate/year 8).

text: This Government's recently announced Go Rural programme offers student teachers $4,000 to cover the cost of undertaking a placement in a rural and isolated school... yesterday I announced a further 87 places per year... We're also increasing the number of places available in the Government's Teacher Bonding Scheme by 50 places to 235 per year, supporting teachers with an additional $40,000 over five years.
explanation: Dense, precise detail: $4,000 placements, 87 extra places, +50 to 235 bonding places, $40,000 over five years, $2.35m/year.

text: It may well be the Green Party policy for a low level of English, and if you've got a criminal record, and if you've got poor health, you can get residence in New Zealand, but that is not the expectation of most New Zealanders.
explanation: Caricatures Green policy as welcoming criminals and the unhealthy — a strawman.

text: What parents do like to talk to me about is the curriculum, and not only the New Zealand curriculum but the refreshed Te Marautanga o Aotearoa, which is an amazing document that we have completely refreshed in under two years, and I would have expected questions around the work we have done on Te Marautanga o Aotearoa rather than a defence of their woeful education record in Government.
explanation: 'Woeful education record' is a partisan jab at the opposition rather than engagement with the question.

text: It was extraordinary that there had been only 47 visits when 13,000 people had been given an exemption from home-schooling, and he asked, "How do we know that any of these kids are getting a good education?" The answer from Jan Tinetti at the time, in 2023, was "I don't think that we do.", and yet they did absolutely nothing about it.
explanation: Criticises predecessor's inaction using her own words; pointed but record-based rather than a personal insult.

text: As I've already said, there will only be a very, very, very small number of people who will go through this process, and if you start talking about the reasons for your decisions, they are potentially going to be identifiable. The select committee already went over this... We're traversing old ground.
explanation: 'We're traversing old ground' is mildly dismissive of the questioner, though not a personal attack.

text: Just to answer that last question: we have to create physical restraint rules for the hostels, hence the delayed commencement.
explanation: Plain, cooperative reply.

text: As I've already stated, the Ministry of Education is gathering that information at the moment. All options are on the table, as of course you would expect in that dynamically shifting environment. We are planning for a range of different scenarios.
explanation: Asked to commit to raising the 27c/km allowance given AT's 80c/km figure; gives no commitment and falls back on 'all options on the table'.

text: There are things in that question that are not linked. Any person who becomes a tax resident in this country has the ability to buy a house, and any person in this country becomes also a resident. What the member seems to be suggesting ... is that there should be the same level of English language for all resident visa holders, and, if that is the case, a refugee who is a partner of a New Zealander should also face these higher English language requirements.
explanation: Rejects the premise and reframes, partly answering by exposing the implication rather than addressing the 'different standards' charge head-on.

text: NCEA has become increasingly fragmented and inconsistent across schools, and too often students have been able to accumulate credits without building the knowledge and skills they need for the future.
explanation: Directly answers why the Government is replacing NCEA.

text: Look, the advice that I've had is that that is not possible. And of course, the whole purpose of this is to remove this part of the bill so that we can then go through a full process and work with the Home Schooling NZ association on their views.
explanation: Directly answers that the suggested administrative route is, per advice, not possible, and states the alternative plan.

text: In answer to those two questions: about consultation, yes; and anything else I'm considering, no.
explanation: Crisp, direct yes/no answers to the two distinct questions asked.

text: The bill limits objections to those who live or work in the local council area or within 1 kilometre of the proposed licence... In one case, a venue spent $45,000 preparing for a hearing that the objector didn't even turn up for.
explanation: Relies on a single anecdote ($45,000 case) to justify a general rule.

text: Alcohol is a legal product. The overwhelming majority of New Zealanders consume it without incident and without imposing costs on others. Where alcohol does cause real harm, violence, disorder, drink-driving, and harm to children, the State has both the right and the duty to act decisively, but restricting the freedom of everyone here because of a minority who behave badly is neither fair nor effective.
explanation: A structured majority/minority and proportionality argument; reasonable but rests on an unquantified 'overwhelming majority' premise.

text: Some parties in this House may support freeing criminals and punishing success, but this Government has flipped the script, and we’re freeing New Zealanders to succeed and making sure the criminals get punished.
explanation: Built on a false dichotomy and strawman with no evidence.

text: Youth crime was completely out of control. There was no encouragement, there was no oversight, there were no kids even going to school. The previous Government left it in the too-hard basket.
explanation: Relies on exaggeration rather than evidence to set up the contrast.

text: This bill makes a series of changes which will free New Zealanders and businesses from the stranglehold of red tape and support economic growth.
explanation: Introduction of a bill is action-in-progress, not delivered reform.

text: The move to a single supervisor in the Department of Internal Affairs will mean clearer accountability, faster guidance, and more reliable support for businesses who are trying to comply with the law. The transition is on track to go live on 1 July 2026
explanation: Stated commitment with a date; follow-through still pending.

text: Most importantly, we've taken the money from the gangs that they have profited from and we are giving it back to the communities in the form of $11.9 million going to the police programme initiative called ROCC—Resilience of Organised Crime in Communities.
explanation: Describes funding allocated to a named initiative; delivery presented as under way.

text: Serious repeat youth offending is down 22 percent, ahead of the 2030 target of a 15 percent reduction. She's got there already. Ram raids are down by 85 percent.
explanation: Claims a target met ahead of schedule, presented as delivered.

text: We have brought back three strikes, but not only have we brought it back, we've added sexual offending as one of the eligible offences for a strike.
explanation: Describes an enacted law change with a specific addition delivered.

text: Today, I announced the first major step in rebuilding New Zealand’s senior secondary qualification, with Cabinet agreeing to major structural decisions to replace NCEA with a new system... The new qualification across years 12 and 13, and the stand-alone foundational award in literacy and numeracy, will be phased from 2028 with a foundational award; 2029 for the year 12 qualification; and 2030 for year 13.
explanation: An announcement of Cabinet decisions with future rollout; structural decision taken but delivery years away, not yet implemented.

text: We will ensure that every single child in this country at primary school will learn to read through structured literacy, and we will ensure that structured mathematics is embedded
explanation: Firm universal commitment; delivery remains to be shown at this point in the term.

text: We are removing distractions from classrooms by banning cellphone use during the school day in order to lift engagement, achievement, and, importantly, wellbeing. We also will ensure students at primary school receive at least one hour of reading, writing, and maths throughout every day.
explanation: Firm commitments stated within the 100-day plan; delivery not yet demonstrated at this point.

text: This Government's recently announced Go Rural programme offers student teachers $4,000 to cover the cost of undertaking a placement in a rural and isolated school... yesterday I announced a further 87 places per year... We're also increasing the number of places available in the Government's Teacher Bonding Scheme by 50 places to 235 per year, supporting teachers with an additional $40,000 over five years.
explanation: Concrete, costed measures, but largely just announced ('yesterday I announced'), so delivery/uptake is still prospective.

text: Through the use of off-site manufactured builds and repeatable classroom designs, we’ve delivered 583 classrooms in 2024—31 percent more than 2023—delivering classrooms to many schools have been waiting for some time.
explanation: Claims concrete past delivery (583 classrooms) with a year-on-year increase, demonstrating follow-through.

text: Earlier this month, I announced that planning is under way for the expansion of locally delivered healthcare services across the Otago Central Lakes region... Our plan will grow primary care, diagnostic services, outpatient services, and mental health and addiction support, alongside further work to develop maternity care, obstetrics, and gynaecology
explanation: An announcement that planning is under way rather than delivered services — early-stage, follow-through unproven.

text: Well, I have raised expectations with the Director-General of Health that advice is made sufficiently clear to both Ministers and the public. Equally, I understand that as a Minister, I’m obligated to question advice as it is presented to me... It is critically important that we have transparency about the information we have in this regard.
explanation: Describes actions taken (raising expectations with the DG) but they are process commitments, not delivered outcomes.

text: Yes. The Government expects all organisations that handle New Zealanders' health information, including private providers, to meet the highest standards to keep that information safe. Following recent incidents involving private digital health providers, I asked the Director-General of Health and the chief executive of Health New Zealand to write to providers across the sector reminding them of their obligations … That's why we invested an additional $9 million in Budget 2024 and a further $10 million in Budget 2025 to strengthen cyber-security capability within Health New Zealand.
explanation: Describes commissioned reviews and funding allocations; concrete steps under way, though outcomes not yet demonstrated.

text: We've banned gang patches, and we've got police back on the beat and have reduced the number of victims of crime by 49,000.
explanation: Claims enacted measures (patch ban) plus a delivery outcome; the 49,000 reduction claim is attributed to government action.

text: This week, I announced that the coalition Government had axed the former Government’s hugely wasteful $16 billion Lake Onslow scheme This decision fulfils another commitment under our coalition Government’s 100-day plan.
explanation: Reports actually cancelling the scheme, fulfilling a stated 100-day commitment — delivery, not just announcement.

text: It was human error. Of course, I take responsibility for all of the things that happen in my office, as you would expect.
explanation: Owns the mistake rather than deflecting; words align with accepting accountability.

text: In response to question No. 3 I said the transport residence pathway was for bus drivers who'd applied for a work visa between September 2023 and April 2024. I meant to say it was for any bus driver who applied for a work visa before 7 April 2024.
explanation: Proactively corrects her own earlier statement on the record — words aligned with accuracy.

text: We are committed to raising achievement and we’re not just talking about it; we’re doing it.
explanation: Claim that words are matched by deeds; partly backed by the specific measures she cited in the same answer, though self-asserted.

text: Their advice to me was that no curriculum learning areas had been developed—directly before I came down to the House. That advice was incorrect, I relied on it, and as soon as I was made aware that they had incorrectly advised me directly before I was down in the House, I made a statement to the House correcting that statement.
explanation: The questioner cites Jan 2024 advice she reportedly signed showing work had begun, creating tension with her 'incorrectly advised' explanation; her account is contested within the exchange.

text: The resident visa 2021 granted residence to nearly 213,000 people, not 230,000 people. And temporary work visas under the Indian free-trade agreement have to have a genuine job offer, but they’re not labour market tested.
explanation: Proactively corrects her own earlier overstatements in the same sitting — bringing her words into line with the facts.

text: instead what we'd see are New Zealand – trained graduate nurses getting on the plane with the tens of thousands of other young New Zealanders who are leaving the country because they do not see a future here. We are in danger of becoming a training ground for Australia when it comes to our medical professionals.
explanation: Predicts continued emigration of NZ-trained nurses; directionally consistent with current outflow trends but magnitude uncertain.

text: I want to, first of all, acknowledge the Iranian people... any family in a conflict zone is in a horrific place, but, of course, the brutal regime that they have had to survive under for some decades is terrible as well.
explanation: Respectful, measured tone that engages the humanitarian substance.

text: Words matter, and we need to dial it back a notch from some of the rhetoric that we've heard on the other side of the House.
explanation: Calls for restraint and lower temperature, though directed pointedly at 'the other side'.

text: Look, I’m happy to offer the previous speaker my pocket square, because he has a large dollop of sad sauce right there on his face.
explanation: Personal mockery of Robertson ('sad sauce on his face') rather than engagement with his argument.

text: it is time to accept that the public have spoken. They have resoundingly told us here in this House that the Labour Government was a failure.
explanation: Blunt 'failure' framing of opponents; harsh but a political characterisation rather than a personal insult.

text: thanks to this Trump-loving, MAGA hat - wearing, Aotearoa-hating, New Zealand First, ACT, and National coalition
explanation: String of personal/character insults ('Aotearoa-hating', 'MAGA hat-wearing') aimed at opponents, not policy.

text: The so-called digital nomad tax exemption stems from some fantasy that this Government has that the way to create a modern, resilient, productive economy is to sell our country to foreign investors. It is selling to them our conservation land, allowing them to buy our houses, and now, apparently, exempting them from the tax regimes in this country.
explanation: Attributes a 'fantasy' motive to the government rather than engaging the policy's stated rationale.

text: This Government, like the French generals of World War II, are fighting the last war.
explanation: Pointed critique of approach via metaphor, not a personal attack.

text: Now, there is one good measure, and I want to front-foot it because I'm a positive guy. I like to start by saying positive things. One good measure that this bill does that we do support is the change to exempt income from selling electricity to the grid. That is a good change.
explanation: Constructive, acknowledges merit in an opponent's bill.

text: We appreciate the helpful, minor tinkering it does around the Working for Families scheme. Those are all good, positive changes.
explanation: Respectful, credits opponents' work.

text: …if she really wants us to be as rich as Australia, I suggest that she supports the Resource Management Act reforms and she also supports fast track and she supports mining. If she does that, we will be richer than Australia.
explanation: Overstated causal claim that backing three policies would make NZ 'richer than Australia' — unsupported leap.

text: there was the same issue prior to this Government, except that it was worse because, under the extensive and overdone lockdowns in Auckland, the home of most Pasifika people in New Zealand, many young people were denied their education... attendance rates were a mere 17 percent.
explanation: Uses a single anecdotal 17% attendance figure from one principal in 2021 to characterise the prior era.

text: we had a situation, that we inherited, of massive inflation, up to over 7 percent. Debt—just the interest rates alone that the Minister of Finance is having to find money for—of $11 billion a year extra every single year; basically, borrowed money paying for borrowed money.
explanation: Blames the prior government for inherited conditions but doesn't connect this to the Pasifika outcomes asked about.

text: I give you, then, international law on the law of the sea and the rights for this country and other countries to be able to have commercial shipping, and we call on Iran to comply with the United Nations Security Council Resolution 2817.
explanation: Grounds the position in a concrete legal instrument rather than rhetoric.

text: …a lot of those, for instance, Fonterra staff employees cannot work from home, because they're working in factories. … Certainly, if we look in the public sector, New Zealand Police front-line staff, Corrections front-line staff, probation officers, nurses, doctors, and teachers do not have that luxury.
explanation: Counters the private-sector analogy with relevant examples of roles that cannot work remotely; reasonable point.

text: It's endorsed and cosigned by many countries that we would typically have strong and close partnerships with—the United Kingdom, France, Netherlands, Canada, Japan. They've all signed on because they also understand the importance of the international rules-based system.
explanation: Supports the case with the fact of broad co-signing, but partly an appeal to the company kept rather than the statement's merits.

text: it is time to accept that the public have spoken. They have resoundingly told us here in this House that the Labour Government was a failure.
explanation: Treats an election result as proof the previous Government 'was a failure' — conflates electoral verdict with substantive judgement.

text: thanks to this Trump-loving, MAGA hat - wearing, Aotearoa-hating, New Zealand First, ACT, and National coalition
explanation: Ad hominem with no evidence offered for the characterisations.

text: This Government, like the French generals of World War II, are fighting the last war.
explanation: Argument by historical analogy; rhetorically apt but does little to establish the claim on its own.

text: We know that 311 of the wealthiest families in Aotearoa already hold more wealth than the bottom 50 percent.
explanation: Uses a concrete statistic to support the inequality argument, though cited loosely.

text: why rush through under urgency when it could have been done through a normal select committee process? It just speaks to the wider trend and the wider thread of this Government, which has really used urgency quite a lot during this term, the most out of any Government, I believe, according to an analysis from Newsroom
explanation: Cites a Newsroom analysis as evidence, though hedged with 'I believe'.

text: countries, like the United States, that are net exporters of oil are being affected by this crisis and are having their fuel prices increase as well, because fossil fuel is a global commodity in traded in global markets, whereas local renewable energy generation, such as this bill is encouraging through the renewable energy income tax exemption, is traded locally and means it’s exempt from the global oil shocks that we are seeing
explanation: Logically sound: uses the US net-exporter case to show domestic refining wouldn't insulate prices, since oil clears globally.

text: That is something that New Zealand has stood in strong support of over many, many years and in many parts of the world. That's why we sent a vessel up through the Taiwan Strait as well.
explanation: NZ did sail a vessel through the Taiwan Strait — substantially accurate.

text: we’ve seen that wait-list for public housing go through the roof, an extra 20,000-odd under the previous Government, despite them saying that housing was going to be one of their key solutions that they first came in on.
explanation: The public housing register did rise by roughly 20,000 over Labour's term; figure is broadly accurate though 'through the roof' adds rhetorical colour.

text: They don't want to know how much racism there is in our community, because under Christopher Luxon it's got worse.
explanation: An unmeasurable and unsupported assertion that racism 'got worse' under a named leader.

text: The Prime Minister himself said any action is justified—that was his first substantive statement—and it was palpably false. It was wrong, and he had to roll it back because he didn't know what he was talking about.
explanation: Reports the PM said action was 'justified' and rolled it back — plausible but partly characterisation, not independently confirmed here.

text: the Key-English Government actually started this work, because the Key-English Government had some faults, but they were genuinely interested in improving the lives of New Zealanders in their conservative, traditional way.
explanation: Broadly accurate that the living-standards/wellbeing work has roots in the Key-English era.

text: here’s one of the things that this Speech from the Throne says: “for the past several years the number of people employed in the public service has grown at a rate that has not been matched by a commensurate increase in the level of services provided to the public.” Does that sound like Christopher Luxon to you? No, that’s the 2008 Speech from the Throne.
explanation: Presents a verifiable textual parallel between the 2008 and 2023 throne speeches; plausible and checkable, though the precise wording match is asserted.

text: This bill has arisen largely out of an Ombudsman's report into conditions at the most maximum security unit at Pāremoremo and his finding, essentially, that the conditions there were inhumane.
explanation: Accurately characterises the origin of the bill and the Ombudsman's adverse findings on Pāremoremo conditions.

text: helpful tinkering would be fine if we weren’t in the middle of the biggest fossil fuel crisis that we’ve ever had, if we weren’t at the highest level of unemployment we’ve ever had, if we weren’t facing an explosive cost of living situation
explanation: Superlative claims ('biggest ever', 'highest unemployment ever') are hyperbole; NZ unemployment is not at a record high.

text: putting a financial package of assistance to 150,000 families out of 1.78 million households in New Zealand—where not even every one of those 150,000 is getting $50 a week—is not enough.
explanation: Figures are specific; the '150,000' differs from other speakers' '143,000/140,000', and full accuracy is unconfirmed.

text: It’s, unfortunately, a half measure because less than half of the children in households in material poverty are actually going to get this relief because more than half—52 percent—are in benefit households.
explanation: Consistent with NZ data that a large share of children in material hardship are in benefit-reliant households; the exact 52% would need sourcing.

text: The Budget Policy Statement does not mention the word “resilience” or the phrase “climate change” even once.
explanation: A specific, checkable claim about the document's contents; plausible and the kind of thing easily verified, though unconfirmed here.

text: Per capita GDP fell 5 percent from its peak in 2022, compared with a fall of 3.9 percent over the 2008 to 2009 period.
explanation: Quoted directly from the Half Year Economic and Fiscal Update; sourced and specific.

text: the members opposite are not going to get away with their political violence lightly.
explanation: Combative us-vs-them framing, not consensus-building.

text: does he think New Zealanders are OK with his Government trading off a place with outstanding universal value for short-term, private profits?
explanation: Rhetorically appeals to one side's values rather than seeking common ground.

text: The leaders of our two biggest parties spent more time telling you who not to vote for, trying to scare people with how things will be under the other lot than they spent time talking about how we build the beautiful future our mokopuna deserve.
explanation: Contrasts a hopeful vision against rivals, but the framing still draws an us-vs-them line between the Greens and the big parties.

text: I'm just sitting in here listening to insults and snaps and barbs being traded and personal insults being made; it always leaves out the actual human people's realities who are at the centre of the violence of an illegal war, and those real lives and the harm on them is quickly forgotten in a tit-for-tat political debate. I abhor that.
explanation: Appeals to shared concern for human lives, though framed as a rebuke of 'the other side'.

text: I genuinely think that across this House there is good faith here. I think maybe this is one of the issues where we don’t have to do political argy-bargy, where we can agree we are all seeking to keep our people safe, especially our young people.
explanation: Explicitly disavows partisan combat and asserts shared good faith across the House — strongly consensus-building.

text: The principle is this: don't say anything that might attract a late night tweet from the White House. New Zealand's once proud, independent foreign policy has under this Government... been reduced to abject servility to the Trump White House.
explanation: Rhetorically sharp for his own side but framed to ridicule rather than persuade across the aisle.

text: I was staggered to hear the ACT Party member saying they’re not even going to support a bill that’s only about transparency and disclosure of modern slavery—slavery—in supply chains.
explanation: Expresses incredulity at the opposing party rather than engaging their reasoning to win them over.

text: if you want to have the free flow of capital around the world, for goodness’ sake, do something about maintaining social licence for that, like actually protecting some basic ethical standards, which is what this bill does. If you don’t, you risk losing public confidence and public support in the very system that you want.
explanation: Appeals to free-market supporters in their own terms to bring them toward the bill rather than dismissing them.

text: That's what they love to do every time they give a speech on agriculture—to sing hymns to our farmers in worship of their wondrousness, and I certainly wouldn't want to compete with them on that.
explanation: Amusing to his own side but framed as us-vs-them ridicule of opponents, not consensus-building.

text: Yes, there are people on both sides of this conflict who do not accept the right of the other to exist—that is the sad truth—but they must not be allowed to prevail.
explanation: Acknowledges fault on both sides and seeks a shared path; measured and bridge-building, though within his own framing.

text: I want to, first of all, acknowledge the Iranian people... any family in a conflict zone is in a horrific place, but, of course, the brutal regime that they have had to survive under for some decades is terrible as well.
explanation: Acknowledges both the Iranian people's suffering and the regime — a balanced, bridging opening.

text: Words matter, and we need to dial it back a notch from some of the rhetoric that we've heard on the other side of the House.
explanation: An appeal for moderation, but one-sided in assigning the excess to opponents.

text: Now, there is one good measure, and I want to front-foot it because I'm a positive guy. I like to start by saying positive things. One good measure that this bill does that we do support is the change to exempt income from selling electricity to the grid. That is a good change.
explanation: Credits the government's measure and leads with the positive — a consensus-building gesture across the aisle.

text: It shows that when you get together and when you work with people, you can make a difference, even in a limited form.
explanation: Inclusive, collaboration-praising message that frames progress as collective rather than partisan.

text: thanks to this Trump-loving, MAGA hat - wearing, Aotearoa-hating, New Zealand First, ACT, and National coalition
explanation: Pure us-vs-them demonisation that alienates rather than persuades the unconvinced.

text: We appreciate the helpful, minor tinkering it does around the Working for Families scheme. Those are all good, positive changes.
explanation: Acknowledges merit in the Government's bill, a bridge-building note across the aisle.

text: The worst thing they could do for homelessness and begging is nothing. It’s the most mana-reducing, soul-destroying thing. The move-on orders actually give our police the tool to plug them in with NGOs, local government, central government agencies and make a difference to their life, because, unlike the Opposition, we’ve actually got aspiration for the most vulnerable people in this country.
explanation: 'Unlike the Opposition, we've actually got aspiration' is a partisan jab that undercuts the consensus framing.

text: The four-phase plan that we've seen, that's now in the public domain, is simple yet pragmatic, and it's so good, even the Australians are starting to copy it.
explanation: Upbeat selling of the Government's plan, but boastful and appealing only to supporters.

text: To all the small-business owners out there, I am one too. I can relate. You are the backbone of the New Zealand economy. Help is coming.
explanation: Builds rapport with a constituency through shared identity, though it appeals to one sector rather than seeking broad common ground.

text: To the coalition and the leadership of Winston Peters and David Seymour, thank you for your integrity and unity to work together cohesively. I look forward to working with you and your MPs as we unite under a broader korowai of mutual values and aspiration for our country.
explanation: Unifying, cooperative language emphasising shared values, though it builds consensus within the governing coalition rather than across the aisle.

text: I would firstly like to thank the people of Hamilton East, the 17,950 people who entrusted me with their vote, and to those who didn't, know that I am still here for you also.
explanation: Inclusive gesture reaching beyond his own voters to those who opposed him, inviting them in rather than dividing.

text: We will be stronger, we will be tougher, and we will be more compassionate. We will be more staunch than we have ever been before
explanation: Pure rallying slogan with no concrete content.

text: There is no civil defence payment opened up for Hokianga and the North right now. Why? Why is their stress not enough?
explanation: Names the place (Hokianga/the North) and the specific support missing, though no figures.

text: We have won marriage equality, stopped the harms of conversion therapy, ended the logging of native timber, revitalised te reo through kōhanga reo and kura kaupapa, decriminalised abortion, and built thousands of warm, dry homes.
explanation: Names concrete reforms and programmes.

text: The Clean Car Discount wound back, the billion dollar liquefied natural gas terminal, the $200 million for fossil fuel companies, a range of energy funds and efficiency funds that have been pulled back, and $20 billion a year on fossil fuels—$29 million a day.
explanation: Dense list of named policies and dollar figures (billion-dollar terminal, $200 million, $20 billion/year, $29 million/day).

text: Our mātāwaka caucus of Māori and Pasifika members of Parliament has grown from three members to seven.
explanation: Exact before/after numbers given.

text: It's endorsed and cosigned by many countries that we would typically have strong and close partnerships with—the United Kingdom, France, Netherlands, Canada, Japan. They've all signed on because they also understand the importance of the international rules-based system.
explanation: Names specific co-signatory partners to substantiate the point.

text: we’ve seen that wait-list for public housing go through the roof, an extra 20,000-odd under the previous Government, despite them saying that housing was going to be one of their key solutions that they first came in on.
explanation: Cites a concrete figure (extra 20,000) for the waitlist increase.

text: in the Waikato we will be in our first 100 days signing a memorandum of understanding with the University of Waikato about establishing a third medical school.
explanation: Names a concrete action (MOU), a named partner, a location and a timeframe (first 100 days).

text: that’s why we’re seeing the first piece of legislation coming through next week helping to get the Reserve Bank back, focused on that core mandate, so that we can get the economy back under control, get that cost of living under control.
explanation: Names a concrete legislative action and timing (next week) re the Reserve Bank mandate, though the economic outcomes are broad.

text: helpful tinkering would be fine if we weren’t in the middle of the biggest fossil fuel crisis that we’ve ever had, if we weren’t at the highest level of unemployment we’ve ever had, if we weren’t facing an explosive cost of living situation
explanation: Sweeping crisis language without figures or mechanisms.

text: countries, like the United States, that are net exporters of oil are being affected by this crisis and are having their fuel prices increase as well, because fossil fuel is a global commodity in traded in global markets, whereas local renewable energy generation, such as this bill is encouraging through the renewable energy income tax exemption, is traded locally and means it’s exempt from the global oil shocks that we are seeing
explanation: Names the mechanism and the specific bill provision (renewable energy income tax exemption).

text: We do know that 150,000 families that do get this are a drop in the bucket in terms of the 1.8 million households all around New Zealand.
explanation: Two concrete figures (150,000 recipient families vs 1.8 million households).

text: putting a financial package of assistance to 150,000 families out of 1.78 million households in New Zealand—where not even every one of those 150,000 is getting $50 a week—is not enough.
explanation: Concrete numerator/denominator and dollar figure to make the proportional point.

text: Per capita GDP fell 5 percent from its peak in 2022, compared with a fall of 3.9 percent over the 2008 to 2009 period.
explanation: Precise figures, periods, and a benchmark comparison.

text: The Greens absolutely will continue to be consistent in wanting us to at least be honest about whose lives are being honoured here and whose lives are being said to have value here.
explanation: Claims a consistent Green position on even-handed condemnation; plausibly matches the party's record but asserted rather than evidenced here.

text: For at least the past three decades, the Greens have consistently set out a pathway to better protect our people and our living systems against the inevitable topple of fossil fuel dependency—a stable planet that we can all be proud of passing on to our mokopuna.
explanation: Claims long-standing consistency and immediately backs it with the historical record (Rod Donald's 2001 vision), supporting the words-match-record claim.

text: It is punishing young people for a platform that should instead be held accountable.
explanation: Consistent with the Greens' stated position to hold platforms responsible rather than restrict users.

text: we utterly condemn all violence—I am a former prevention of violence Minister—of course, and have since the start condemned all violence, including the attacks by Hamas on 7 October
explanation: Claims a consistent anti-violence position grounded in her ministerial record; plausible and self-consistent within the text.

text: remember that under Labour's Helen Clark, New Zealand stayed out of the United States and the UK and Australia's disastrous invasion of Iraq in 2003
explanation: Invokes Labour's record of independent foreign policy to back the party's current stance — consistent with its history.

text: Speaking in the debate on the first reading of the Immigration (Enhanced Risk Management) Amendment Bill, I incorrectly asserted that Erica Stanford had attended a five countries immigration ministers meeting. I withdraw that statement.
explanation: Voluntarily corrects and withdraws his own earlier false assertion — words being brought into line with the record.

text: This is a very important issue, and I would march in the street on this issue—but that’s probably not saying much, because I would march in the street on lots of different issues.
explanation: Self-aware, self-deprecating candour that acknowledges his own activist disposition rather than overstating the gesture's significance.

text: That is something that New Zealand has stood in strong support of over many, many years and in many parts of the world. That's why we sent a vessel up through the Taiwan Strait as well.
explanation: Argues the current stance is consistent with NZ's longstanding freedom-of-navigation record, citing the Taiwan Strait transit.

text: we’ve seen that wait-list for public housing go through the roof, an extra 20,000-odd under the previous Government, despite them saying that housing was going to be one of their key solutions that they first came in on.
explanation: Attacks Labour's words-vs-record on housing — a low-authenticity signal about opponents, not the speaker.

text: this comes on top of yesterday's announcement of another 2,500 electric vehicle chargers up and down the country. It comes on top of our liquefied natural gas facility in New Plymouth to ensure electricity security into the future.
explanation: Claims credit for energy initiatives, but these are announcements as much as delivered outcomes.

text: This is the Government that’s making Auckland Transport more accountable to Auckland ratepayers. It’s transferring most of Auckland Transport’s functions back to Auckland Council.
explanation: Points to a reform being enacted via the bill at second reading; delivery is in progress.

text: the inevitable legacy of this United States - Israel war against Iran, which will be generations of extremism and anti-Western terrorism, will be directed at New Zealanders.
explanation: Directionally plausible long-run prediction of blowback, but 'inevitable' and 'generations' overstate certainty and magnitude.

text: Bombing people into oblivion will simply breed extremism.
explanation: Prediction that military action will generate further extremism; consistent with much expert opinion but inherently uncertain.

text: We are a broad based – low rate party. We are not looking to increase tax. We are looking to increase economic growth, and that is the priority on this side of the Chamber.
explanation: The 'broad based' label sits in tension with the Government's refusal to tax capital gains, a contradiction Russell directly highlights; words and the stated policy don't fully cohere.

text: these changes that we're making today are real action after a long period of time of non-delivery. Aucklanders, at long last, are going to get back the power that they rightfully deserve in regards to planning and dealing with transport in their city.
explanation: Frames passing the bill as fulfilling a promise; consistent with the Government's stated agenda, though delivery of outcomes is unproven.

text: Has the Government considered a land value tax? No. Has the Government considered a capital gains tax? No. Has the Government considered a death tax? No. Has the Government considered a whole lot of taxes that one wants to make up off the cuff? No.
explanation: Rallies his own side around 'points of difference between the sides of the House'; effective but us-vs-them, not consensus-building.

text: We are a party and a Government of fiscal discipline. We think about where we spend taxpayer money—because it's not our money; it's taxpayer money
explanation: A confident framing aimed at his own base ('taxpayer money'); rhetorically tidy but not consensus-seeking.

text: No. Quite simply, the Government is not considering increasing taxes for hard-working Kiwis; quite the opposite. We're wanting to create a broad based - low rate tax system to encourage economic growth.
explanation: Appeals to 'hard-working Kiwis' for his own side; not aimed at persuading opponents or finding common ground.

text: What a great day it is for Auckland today—what a great day. We are restoring democratic accountability to transport in our biggest city.
explanation: Energetic but appeals to his own side rather than seeking cross-party common ground.

text: On this side of the House, surprisingly, we don’t believe that the only way in which we can help New Zealanders is by writing blank cheques and spraying money everywhere and, hopefully, it hits a target. On this side of the House, we apply a little bit of substance, which is called fiscal discipline.
explanation: Mocking, partisan framing rather than persuasion.

text: Well, it’s about co-investing to ensure we actually get indigenous gas out of the ground, and, ultimately, this Government is actually backing business and backing industry.
explanation: Tension between his earlier 'won't be picking winners' and a $200m subsidy for new fossil-fuel production; answer asserts consistency but does not resolve the apparent inconsistency.

text: The sector has been calling out for this change since 2022. We heard their calls, and we have delivered.
explanation: Frames the action as matching what the sector requested.

text: we expect our health system to treat New Zealanders based on their need, not based on their ethnicity. We have been very clear that we do not agree with having a co-governed health system, which was what the previous Government was delivering and which we have reversed.
explanation: States a position consistent with the Government's actual action of reversing the co-governed health arrangements — words match deeds.

text: Just this term alone, we have reinstated the faster cancer treatment health target; given a $604 million boost to Pharmac... delivering 33 new cancer treatments; expanded breast screening to women aged 70 to 74... and we acknowledge there is still much more work to be done.
explanation: Tempers the achievements with 'there is still much more work to be done', avoiding overclaim.

text: In answer to question No. 6 yesterday, I said that vaccine mandates and workplace settings for the 12- to 17-year age group remained in place until late January 2022. This was based on written Ministry of Health advice which the ministry has since acknowledged was incorrect as it related to booster mandates rather than the primary two-dose series. The correct position is that these mandates remained in place until 4 April 2022.
explanation: Voluntarily corrects his own prior statement to the House; words brought into line with the record.

text: Well, as we know, the unemployment rate is where Treasury forecast it would be, and, as I accept, it is higher than anyone would like. For any individual who finds themselves without a job, it’s incredibly difficult for them and their family.
explanation: Acknowledges an unwelcome reality rather than denying it.

text: Well, I refute that. I've never used that expression in terms of the recipients or the people affected by this bill. There is no change in terms of what currently happens. … They have a responsibility to taxpayers to repay that debt, and MSD, when they have conversations about when a debt has been created, they talk to the person about how that debt can be repaid and over what period.
explanation: Denies ever using 'double dipping'; from the text alone the consistency of this denial cannot be verified.

text: Yes. Our Government has always acknowledged that many Kiwis have been finding it tough during a prolonged cost of living challenge.
explanation: Reaffirms a prior position consistently, though without visible new action backing the acknowledgement.

text: I reject the assertion that we are cutting income support. We are making a change in the way that social housing is delivered.
explanation: Reframing a reduction in temporary additional support as 'not cutting income support' sits in tension with the announced $10.82/week reduction.

text: National will take six weeks to sort coalition. Willis is”—a derogatory word—“and can’t do simple sums.
explanation: Unverifiable anonymous, second-hand claim presented to suggest insiders doubt Willis.

text: What advice has he received or requested regarding Auckland's skyrocketing level of unemployment, now twice what it was three years ago, and the correlation between job losses in Auckland and homelessness?
explanation: 'Twice what it was three years ago' is a strong specific claim about Auckland unemployment that cannot be verified from the text and may be hyperbolic ('skyrocketing').

text: The only growth that we've seen is the growth in unemployment, the growth in business liquidations, and the growth in the number of Kiwis leaving for Australia and other countries because the opportunities are simply not here.
explanation: Unemployment, liquidations and outward migration did rise in this period; the 'only growth' rhetorical absolute overstates it.

text: Was the Prime Minister wrong when he said in May last year that “Unemployment is just almost peaking and about to come down.”, given there are now more people on jobseeker support than at the height of COVID-19?
explanation: Quotes a prior PM statement and contrasts it with current jobseeker numbers; the COVID-height comparison is broadly defensible.

text: Is it a sign of green shoots when the number of young people—18- to 24-year-olds—on jobseeker has grown by 32 percent on her watch, as reported by Radio New Zealand?
explanation: Specific, sourced figure (32 percent, RNZ) used as a factual challenge.

text: Yes, we are disestablishing the Ministry for the Environment, but for very good reason... This merger is simply about reducing bloated bureaucracy. We saw, under the previous Government, something like 16,000 extra bureaucrats were appointed.
explanation: The public-service growth figure is roughly in line with reported numbers but is selectively framed and hedged ('something like').

text: the ministry has actually produced a record amount of output—a full 4,822 items, which included 896 briefings, probably most to Chris Bishop; 62 Cabinet papers, probably most to Chris Bishop; 452 Official Information Act requests, that's probably a lot for you, Andrew Hoggard!; and many, many more parliamentary questions and pieces of ministerial correspondence.
explanation: Precise figures attributed to the select committee report; plausible and sourced, not independently verified here.

text: if you think inflation is bad in the urban environment, go out on-farm. At 16 percent, it is making life miserable.
explanation: On-farm input inflation peaked around the mid-teens percent in 2022-23, so the figure is in the right range, if presented at its peak.

text: The latest Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) forecasts show that food and fibre exports remain at historically high levels, with horticulture alone expected to reach $9.2 billion in revenue this year.
explanation: Cites MPI forecasts with a specific number; presented as official forecast.

text: That's why we've extended the upper age for funded breast screening from 69 to 74, delivering on an election commitment. Since the roll-out began, more than half of the 31,800 women invited for screening have been screened, and 190 breast cancers have been detected
explanation: Concrete, internally consistent rollout figures consistent with the announced policy.

text: Is he delivering the brighter future he promised Pasifika, when almost 10,000 more Pasifika children are living in hardship now, under his watch?
explanation: Embedded claim of ~10,000 more Pasifika children in hardship; specific figure used as challenge.

text: When people put through their submissions to the main Act, 98.7 percent of those submissions to the Finance and Expenditure Committee opposed the bill.
explanation: Overwhelming submission opposition to the Regulatory Standards Bill is well documented; the exact percentage is a precise claim that cannot be fully verified from the text.

text: schedule 8 of the notice alone tells us that it would exclude about 175 instruments on the basis that they are administrative and have no ongoing public impact.
explanation: Specific, checkable factual claim drawn from committee papers; plausible and sourced, though the exact figure is unverified here.

text: the Labour Party opposed the Regulatory Standards Bill. We opposed it at first reading, at second reading, and we also opposed it at third reading.
explanation: Straightforward, checkable account of the party's voting record.

text: section 7(3) provides that a notice can only be issued and take effect after it has been approved by the House of Representatives. In other words, the executive does not get to say the final word on what is excluded from the Act’s consistency assessments, the law’s review obligations, or scrutiny by the Regulatory Standards Board—Parliament does.
explanation: Accurate description of the statutory mechanism and its constitutional effect (House approval required).

text: Does he agree with analysis from Te Kāhui Raraunga that replacing the five-yearly census with administrative data, small-sample surveys, and targeted data collection “will build in a bias that favours numerically dominant groups, and will further invisibilise some Māori individuals, whānau, and communities”?
explanation: Cites a named source and a precise methodological concern.

text: the reforms that are before Parliament failed to address the root cause of our declining fisheries: namely overfishing, over allocation, destructive fishing practises that have persisted for far too long.
explanation: Names concrete mechanisms (overfishing, over-allocation, destructive practices) but no figures.

text: Yet here we are, giving more fish to commercial interests, making it easier for them to catch more with less oversight, blocking camera footage on boats, legalising the dumping of fish.
explanation: Lists concrete claimed effects of the reform (camera footage, dumping, oversight).

text: we will be targeting as our first port of call the great nation of India.
explanation: Names a concrete trade priority (India FTA) but no mechanism or timeframe.

text: We understand that there are about $10 billion in non-tariff barriers sitting on the table that that previous Government ignored for six years.
explanation: Attaches a dollar figure to a named problem area.

text: Yes, we are disestablishing the Ministry for the Environment, but for very good reason... This merger is simply about reducing bloated bureaucracy. We saw, under the previous Government, something like 16,000 extra bureaucrats were appointed.
explanation: Names the new ministry rationale and a figure (≈16,000 extra staff).

text: the ministry has actually produced a record amount of output—a full 4,822 items, which included 896 briefings, probably most to Chris Bishop; 62 Cabinet papers, probably most to Chris Bishop; 452 Official Information Act requests, that's probably a lot for you, Andrew Hoggard!; and many, many more parliamentary questions and pieces of ministerial correspondence.
explanation: Itemised output counts (4,822 items; 896 briefings; 62 Cabinet papers; 452 OIAs).

text: That's why we've extended the upper age for funded breast screening from 69 to 74, delivering on an election commitment. Since the roll-out began, more than half of the 31,800 women invited for screening have been screened, and 190 breast cancers have been detected
explanation: Exact age change, invitation numbers, and cancers detected.

text: Does he agree with analysis from Te Kāhui Raraunga that replacing the five-yearly census with administrative data, small-sample surveys, and targeted data collection “will build in a bias that favours numerically dominant groups, and will further invisibilise some Māori individuals, whānau, and communities”?
explanation: Frames a substantive statistical-bias argument grounded in cited analysis.

text: the reforms that are before Parliament failed to address the root cause of our declining fisheries: namely overfishing, over allocation, destructive fishing practises that have persisted for far too long.
explanation: Identifies named causal drivers and argues the reforms miss them; reasoned, though the causal claims are asserted rather than evidenced here.

text: There are a range of opinions that are proffered in relation to the steps that we have taken in order to address the root causes of homelessness... Finally, some people say and advise of things that would work. Well, guess what? The oil and gas ban didn’t work, and you thought it would.
explanation: Dismisses official advice by appeal to favourable anecdotes and an irrelevant analogy to the oil and gas ban.

text: I’m not across the $2,000 matter, but what I am across are the walks that I go on with community housing providers and councils throughout the country, who have said that the actions that this Government have taken, particularly since the announcement of the Housing First 300 places, funded in September 2025, have made a considerable and material impact on the lives of many Kiwis.
explanation: Relies on anecdotal endorsements from his own walks rather than data on the move-on policy asked about.

text: They have told me directly that the investment announced in September is making a huge and material difference to whānau rough sleeping. My officials shared with me this week an example about a gentleman they met who, through Government tautoko, a provider has supported through immediate access into a warm home.
explanation: Relies on a single anecdote and provider testimony rather than outcome data to evidence 'huge and material difference'.

text: Yes, we are going to charge foreigners to go on some tracks around the country. That's OK, because, actually, when we go to Hawaii and when we go to the United States and when we go to Australia and other places, we pay to go into the national parks.
explanation: Justifies the charge by analogy to overseas parks; reasonable but an appeal to analogy rather than analysis.

text: Wilding pines crowd out native species, damage fragile habitats, alter water flows, and permanently change open natural environments. This investment will help protect some of our most environmentally significant and special areas for future generations.
explanation: Claims grounded in real ecological effects; conclusion about the value of control follows.

text: The latest Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) forecasts show that food and fibre exports remain at historically high levels, with horticulture alone expected to reach $9.2 billion in revenue this year.
explanation: Reports favourable export performance, but the government's causal role in it is asserted.

text: A good example of this was last week’s announcement of an agricultural cooperation arrangement with Chile, which boosts closer collaboration between two exporting nations, reinforces our shared commitment to open, rules-based trade
explanation: Points to a delivered diplomatic arrangement as evidence of follow-through.

text: That's why we've extended the upper age for funded breast screening from 69 to 74, delivering on an election commitment. Since the roll-out began, more than half of the 31,800 women invited for screening have been screened, and 190 breast cancers have been detected
explanation: A specific commitment described as enacted and producing measurable results (190 cancers detected).

text: We provided Pharmac with a $604 million boost, enabling access to new cancer medicines like Keytruda and Enhertu, and we reinstated faster cancer treatment targets to ensure patients are seen sooner.
explanation: Points to a delivered funding boost and named medicines now accessible, plus reinstated targets — concrete action, not just aspiration.

text: we will be targeting as our first port of call the great nation of India.
explanation: An aspiration to prioritise an India deal; no delivery at this point.

text: we’ve taken strong steps to restore law and order, with 49,000 fewer victims of violent crime; ram raids are down 85 percent; and repeat youth offending is down 22 percent... lifting childhood immunisations to 82.6 percent... We are seeing progress in education, with phonics proficiency lifting from 36 percent to 58 percent.
explanation: Cites delivered outcomes, though attribution to Pacific peoples' lives specifically is loose.

text: There’s an inverse relationship between hardship and warm, dry homes. I’m very proud of the Our Whare Our Fale initiative, which, in Porirua, will deliver 300 homes, of which more than a dozen I’ve already enabled.
explanation: Of a 300-home target only 'more than a dozen' are enabled—mostly aspiration, little delivered.

text: National will take six weeks to sort coalition. Willis is”—a derogatory word—“and can’t do simple sums.
explanation: Reads aloud an anonymous text using a slur and mockery of a named opponent's competence — a personal attack delivered by proxy.

text: We've had Nicola Willis in the media, talking about the 8,700 jobs that she intends to cut from the public sector almost gleefully, excited that she's going to take jobs away from 8,700 New Zealanders, impacting 8,700 families.
explanation: Imputes malicious motive ('gleefully', 'excited') to an opponent.

text: Was the Prime Minister wrong when he said in May last year that “Unemployment is just almost peaking and about to come down.”, given there are now more people on jobseeker support than at the height of COVID-19?
explanation: Challenges a forecast on the record, harsh but legitimate.

text: I just want to thank the honourable member Simeon Brown because... he did a fantastic job of selling and re-announcing our three free GP visits. Well done, Simeon Brown. We might need to put you on the payroll.
explanation: Sarcastic but good-humoured jab, not a personal insult.

text: can I acknowledge the new Speaker of the House and all of the presiding officers. We hope for only one thing: that there will be fairness and clarity in the rulings that are undertaken here.
explanation: Respectful, constructive acknowledgement of the Speaker with a reasonable expectation of fairness.

text: Is he delivering the brighter future he promised Pasifika, when almost 10,000 more Pasifika children are living in hardship now, under his watch?
explanation: Holds the Minister to his own promise; harsh but legitimate.

text: I want to be clear that Labour’s support for the select committee’s recommendation today is not an endorsement of the Regulatory Standards Act; it is a recognition that while the Act is on our statute book, section 7’s exclusion mechanism is a safety valve that should be used and should be used well.
explanation: Constructive, respectful framing focused on the merits of the mechanism.

text: I want to begin by thanking the Regulations Review Committee, chaired most ably by my colleague Arena Williams. It is also a committee where we usually agree on most things.
explanation: Collegial, respectful acknowledgement of the committee and its work.

text: The traditional five-yearly survey model is no longer financially sustainable, operationally reliable, or able to produce timely, high-quality data... I do acknowledge the concerns raised by Te Kāhui Raraunga; this Government takes these concerns seriously... Stats New Zealand is committed to working with iwi Māori, including Te Kāhui Raraunga, on the design, planning, and implementation of the new census approach.
explanation: Acknowledges the critics' concerns as legitimate and invites them into the process—bridge-building.

text: I do acknowledge those concerns and have also demonstrated the actions that we’re taking to address them.
explanation: Acknowledges the concerns rather than dismissing them, but offers little substance.

text: I think across a political career, roughly 30 to 50 percent of MPs have their bills drawn from the ballot box, so congratulations for working it up, getting it through caucus, and then getting it drawn.
explanation: Gracious congratulation of an opposition member while explaining the achievement.

text: On 12 March 2026, I stated, “We have seen nearly 5,500 Māori come off the jobseeker benefit in the quarter ending September 2025.” I should have said, “We have seen nearly 5,500 Māori come off the jobseeker into work for the quarter ending September 2025.”
explanation: Voluntarily corrects his own earlier statement on the record, aligning words with the actual data — a consistency-positive act.

text: Yes, I stand by the Government’s track record on Māori employment, particularly given that between 5,000 and 6,000 Māori came off the jobseeker benefit and into work in the quarter ending September 2025—a fantastic result, in my view.
explanation: Defends a stated position consistent with his earlier (corrected) claim.

text: It was like groundhog day. I do support Māori trade training, and what I also support is making sure that the reset of Whānau Ora actually encourages more navigators than the previous Government encouraged.
explanation: Claims to 'support Māori trade training' while his Government defunded a programme an evaluation said exceeded expectations — a words-vs-actions tension raised in the question.

text: I absolutely have confidence in the Minister for Oceans and Fisheries because he has listened to feedback and changed course. He’s listened to what people out there are saying and actually adapted his course to do the right thing.
explanation: Frames a policy reversal as principled responsiveness; defensible but spins a U-turn as virtue.

text: In our party campaign, we said it’s not sustainable to have one ally that spends twice as much and expect them to help us when we won’t help ourselves.
explanation: Links current defence spending action to a stated campaign position; words appear consistent with the policy direction.

text: we campaigned and won an agreement to remove that three by three storey house rule, and it will be gone.
explanation: Action matches ACT's campaign position; words and deeds are consistent here.

text: we have a Resource Management Act currently before select committee, coming back to this House soon, that will put property rights at the centre of resource management law. That is an ACT Party achievement.
explanation: Consistent with ACT's long-standing position on RMA reform and property rights.

text: I announced this policy as ACT’s housing policy in 2016, much closer to when I was visiting Whangārei Hospital... Back then, we called it GST sharing. The spirit of that is here.
explanation: Claims a position held consistently since 2016 now being enacted; words match a long-standing record.

text: there are people with some concerns about disestablishing the ministry, but, again, let's just look at the facts. There are no substantive changes to the functions, there is no reduction in environmental protection, and the changes are structural.
explanation: 'No reduction in environmental protection' is an assertion contested by officials referenced in the question; presented as settled fact.

text: there have been no enduring benefits for the over $200 million that has been wasted by the previous Government on this failed experiment.
explanation: Te Pūkenga establishment costs were substantial, but the precise $200m+ figure and "no enduring benefits" are contestable characterisations.

text: I note that the Stats New Zealand Research and Development Survey shows that employment in the sector increased from 28,200 roles in 2022 to 30,600 roles in 2024, with most of that growth in the private sector... Budget 2025 committed more than $1.8 billion to science and innovation.

text: We know that around 143,000 families will receive the full $50 weekly increase. That will include 48 percent of children in material hardship. The policy is targeted, timely, and temporary to minimise inflation.

text: Based on the most recent figures published by Stats New Zealand, 48 percent of all children in material hardship—around 81,000—are in working households. explanation: Corrected claim is sourced to Stats NZ and carefully caveated about eligibility.

text: Well, the member will have to wait to see at Budget time.
explanation: Asked for a commitment on funding universities and polytechnics; defers entirely without answering.

explanation: Declines to answer the food-bank funding question, citing Budget confidentiality, while pivoting to a different policy.

text: I note that the Stats New Zealand Research and Development Survey shows that employment in the sector increased from 28,200 roles in 2022 to 30,600 roles in 2024, with most of that growth in the private sector... Budget 2025 committed more than $1.8 billion to science and innovation.
explanation: Affirms her statement and supplies data but sidesteps the specific job-loss figure the question put to her.

text: there are people with some concerns about disestablishing the ministry, but, again, let's just look at the facts. There are no substantive changes to the functions, there is no reduction in environmental protection, and the changes are structural.
explanation: Asked why her view differs from official advice; gives her position but doesn't engage the cited advice directly.

text: the unique residential agricultural training facility Telford will be receiving $2.4 million to address deferred maintenance to ensure a fit for purpose, fully functioning agricultural campus.

text: We are fixing the basics and building the future of the West Coast.
explanation: A repeated slogan with no figures, mechanism or measurable commitment.

text: We will work through this disestablishment sensibly and calmly, working a process in consultation with staff, with students, with community, and with industry.
explanation: Names the stakeholders to consult but no mechanism, timeframe or end-state.

text: This Government has put in place extra Youth Guarantee places, an extra 175 places this year, to a total of 8,400 young people who participated in Youth Guarantee schemes over 2025; Apprenticeship Boost, which subsidises employers—over $25 million was spent on Apprenticeship Boost through Vote Social Development.
explanation: Specific place counts (175, 8,400) and spending figure ($25m) for named schemes.

text: From 1 January, NorthTec will be reestablished as a stand-alone regional polytechnic.
